source.title: AI Agent tool observations return the literal empty string under executionOrder "v0"

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

When an AI Agent node runs in a workflow with `settings.executionOrder: "v0"`, every tool call in the turn produces the two-character string `""` as its observation in `intermediateSteps`. The tool node itself executes successfully and its real output is present in the saved execution data, but the agent never sees it. The LLM then either hallucinates a plausible value or reports that the tool returned nothing. No error is raised. The workflow produces a wrong answer silently.

The failure is deterministic under v0, not intermittent. Every tool call in the turn gets the empty observation, on every execution.

Root cause, confirmed by source read and A/B test:

- In `packages/core/src/execution-engine/requests-response.ts`, `handleRequest` builds `nodesToBeExecuted` and inserts the resumed agent entry via an unconditional `nodesToBeExecuted.unshift(...)` at around line 277. The `executionOrder === 'v1'` check at line 271 only guards the `reverse()` of the tool entries above it.
- Under v1: reverse at 271, then unshift at 277, then `addNodeToBeExecuted` also enqueues with `unshift` into the stack (`workflow-execute.ts:481`). The two inversions cancel, tools drain first, the agent resumes after.
- Under v0: no reverse, same unshift at 277, but `addNodeToBeExecuted` enqueues with `push`. The resume entry ends up at the front of a FIFO drain and pops before any tool runs.
- `initializeNodeRunData` (`requests-response.ts:55-86`) pre-creates a placeholder run slot for each tool, with `inputOverride`, `source`, `executionIndex: 0`, `executionTime: 0`, `startTime: 0`, and no `data` field.
- `collectSubNodeResults` (`workflow-execute.ts:1901-1918`) only checks whether the slot exists, not whether it has `.data`. Under v0 the agent reads the placeholder.
- `buildObservation` in `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/utils/agent-execution/buildSteps.ts` (around lines 373-389) finds no `ai_tool` output, no error, and falls through to `JSON.stringify('')` at line 388.

Evidence from a 4-node reproduction on 2.46.6, same workflow, same prompt, same credential, only `settings.executionOrder` changed between the two groups:

| executionOrder | agent executionIndex | tool executionIndex | tool start minus last LLM call end | observation length |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v0 | 3 | 5 | +6 ms | 2 chars (`""`) |
| v0 | 3 | 5 | +5 ms | 2 chars (`""`) |
| v0 | 3 | 5 | +6 ms | 2 chars (`""`) |
| v1 | 4 | 3 | -1974 ms | 1656 chars |
| v1 | 4 | 3 | -1945 ms | 1656 chars |
| v1 | 4 | 3 | -2091 ms | 1656 chars |

Same measurement on a 110-node production workflow showed +305 ms under v0.

The correlation in the failing executions is correct. Right node name, right runIndex, right `toolCallId`. The saved `runData['Gmail MCP'][0].data.ai_tool[0][0].json` contains 3790 characters of real payload. The observation is still `""`.

Not specific to one tool type. Reproduces with `mcpClientTool` against Gmail, Google Contacts, data.gouv.fr, Firecrawl, and with `toolWorkflow` calling SerpAPI. Not auth-related: reproduces on public MCP servers with no auth. Not model-related: reproduces on gpt-4.1-mini with `responsesApiEnabled: false`.

Why this matters for users who didn't write the workflow by hand: workflows created through the public REST API, imported, or generated via the CLI or SDK without an explicit `executionOrder` fall back to v0. Workflows created in the editor get v1 and do not hit this. The editor does not warn anyone that an AI Agent in a v0 workflow will silently receive empty tool results.

Likely fix direction (for triage, not part of this report): make the resume insertion at `requests-response.ts:277` order-aware, using `unshift` under v1 and `push` under v0. Two lines of code. The v0 test at `requests-response.test.ts:549-593` currently asserts the buggy order `['AI Agent', 'Tool A', 'Tool B']` and would need updating to `['Tool A', 'Tool B', 'AI Agent']`. A regression test for v0 + agent + tool + correct observation does not exist today.

Disclosure: this issue was filed after investigation in #38870, where the mechanism was confirmed on a reproduction by @lwiart and the source was cross-checked by several people in that thread. The original reporter of #38870 is on v1 and that issue is separate.



### To Reproduce

1. Create a 4-node workflow: Chat Trigger, an AI Agent node (v3.1) with a language model (e.g. `lmChatOpenAi`) and one tool (e.g. `mcpClientTool` pointed at a public server such as https://mcp.data.gouv.fr/mcp, or a `toolWorkflow` calling any sub-workflow).
2. Enable `returnIntermediateSteps: true` on the AI Agent node, or set `forceToolCallOnFirstIteration: true` so the tool is called on every run.
3. Set the workflow's `settings.executionOrder` to `"v0"`. The easiest way is to import a workflow JSON with that setting, or create the workflow via the public API without an explicit executionOrder (which also falls back to v0).
4. Trigger the agent with a prompt that causes it to call the tool.
5. Inspect `intermediateSteps[0].observation` in the agent's execution result. It will be the two-character string `""`.
6. Inspect the tool node's own execution data via `GET /rest/executions/<id>`. It will show `executionStatus: "success"` and `data.ai_tool[0][0].json` populated with the real payload.
7. Change only `settings.executionOrder` to `"v1"`, keep the same workflow, prompt, and credential. Repeat. The observation is now correct.

### Expected behavior

`intermediateSteps[i].observation` for a tool call should contain the tool's real output whenever the tool node executed successfully. It should never be the literal `""` when the tool produced a result.

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: The reported ordering is consistent with the current source: `handleRequest` reverses requested nodes only for v1, then unconditionally prepends the resumed node; `addNodeToBeExecuted` uses `unshift` for v1 but `push` for v0. That makes the resume entry eligible before the requested tool entries under v0. A targeted regression should assert the resumed agent runs only after the tool output is available under v0 (and that the observation contains that output), not just assert the queue order. This also protects against changing the ordering in a way that breaks multi-tool requests.

comments.author: blucca
comments.text:
Thanks for pinning down the `executionOrder` distinction. It exposed a related regression-harness bug in my n8n-check runner: cloning a workflow filled an omitted setting with `v1`.

Fixed in [0.1.8](https://github.com/blucca/n8n-check/releases/tag/v0.1.8). The harness keeps omission, `v0`, and `v1` as exported. In a credential-free native n8n 2.41.7 branch control, both runs return identical items, while Upper/Lower execution indices reverse (3/2 versus 2/3). Both item checks pass.

[Runnable fixture and recorded indices](https://github.com/blucca/n8n-check/tree/v0.1.8/examples/execution-order).

For Agent/model/tool graphs, the [current fixture scope](https://github.com/blucca/n8n-check/blob/12cfcb1/README.md#L289) is a self-contained standard-node portion; independent AI dependencies produce a named preparation error.

How are you testing API-generated workflows before activating them?

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: The v0 failure mechanism is still present at current HEAD: `handleRequest()` reverses requested tool entries only for v1, then unconditionally prepends the resumed node at `requests-response.ts:277`. Since the v0 execution stack drains with `push`, the resumed agent can run before those tools. One useful edge case for the regression is a request with multiple tools: assert each tool has populated `.data` before the agent resumes, and that each observation contains its corresponding result. Queue order alone would not catch a placeholder being mistaken for completed output.

comments.author: techaurah
comments.text: Verified the reported mechanism against current main (HEAD 0ab1817) by reading the source. It checks out exactly as reported: in packages/core/src/execution-engine/requests-response.ts the reverse at line 272 runs only under executionOrder v1, while the resume unshift at line 277 is unconditional; addNodeToBeExecuted enqueues with unshift under v1 and push under v0; initializeNodeRunData pre-creates a placeholder run slot with inputOverride, source and zeroed timings but no data field; collectSubNodeResults in workflow-execute.ts (line 2064) only checks whether the slot exists, not whether it has data; and buildObservation in packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/utils/agent-execution/buildSteps.ts falls through to JSON.stringify('') at line 411. I also confirmed the v0 test in requests-response.test.ts still asserts the buggy order ['AI Agent', 'Tool A', 'Tool B']. On the question in my earlier comment: the ordering fix itself lives in packages/core, so it needs a maintainer or collaborator. A change outside core cannot deliver the real output, because under v0 the tool genuinely has not run yet when the agent resumes; at most buildObservation could avoid emitting the misleading empty string. I verified the mechanism by source read on current main, not by a live run, since that needs a full n8n plus agent plus MCP setup.
